lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: unit squares and area as a count of squares
lessonRef.title: Concept build A: unit squares and area as a count of squares

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Study both examples. The second one drops some of the wording of the first.

items.prompt: Which statement correctly describes the perimeter of a shape?

steps: Perimeter is the distance around the outside boundary of a shape, measured in linear units, not the space it covers.
workedSolution.answer: Perimeter is the distance around the outside edge of a shape, measured in linear units.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching adult. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Which statement correctly describes the area of a shape?
choices: Area is always the same number as the perimeter for any rectangle.
Area can be found by counting only the unit squares along one edge of a shape.
Area is the distance around the outside edge of a shape, measured in linear units.
Area is the amount of flat space a shape covers, measured in square units.

items.prompt: A student is explaining what area measures. Which statement is correct?
choices: Area is the amount of flat space a shape covers, measured in square units.
Area can be found by counting only the unit squares along one edge of a shape.
Area is always the same number as the perimeter for any rectangle.
Area is the distance around the outside edge of a shape, measured in linear units.

items.prompt: Which statement could be used to define area in square units?
choices: Area is always the same number as the perimeter for any rectangle.
Area is the distance around the outside edge of a shape, measured in linear units.
Area can be found by counting only the unit squares along one edge of a shape.
Area is the amount of flat space a shape covers, measured in square units.
